```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  width = 78
)
helper_candidates <- c(
  "cpi-chart-example.R",
  file.path("vignettes", "cpi-chart-example.R")
)
helper <- helper_candidates[file.exists(helper_candidates)][[1L]]
source(helper)
cpi <- NULL
if (requireNamespace("testthat", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cpi <- statsnz_example_cpi()
}
```

`statsnzreleases` turns selected Stats NZ information-release attachments into
standardised time-series tables. This guide follows a complete workflow:
discover a supported family, retrieve representative official CPI series
through the public reader, chart the `period_date` and `data_value` columns,
and retain provenance for later reproduction.

## Which Stats NZ access path does this guide use?

This guide uses Stats NZ's information-release path, not the Aotearoa Data
Explorer data API. `statsnz_latest_release()` calls a separate,
credential-free release-calendar endpoint on `www.stats.govt.nz`; the reader
then fetches the selected release page and its attached official files. It
does not send a Data Explorer query or use an API subscription key.

Use the [Aotearoa Data Explorer API guide](https://portal.apis.stats.govt.nz/api-guide)
when you need a custom dimensional query from a dataset published there. Use
this package when you need one of its supported published-release file
workflows, standardised output, and attachment-level provenance. The Source
coverage article describes this boundary and the package's behaviour as Stats
NZ continues moving datasets between dissemination systems.

## 1. Discover a supported release family

The release registry is packaged with the installed package, so this first
step works without a network connection.  Use `include_unsupported = FALSE`
when you want only families that the current release can import.

```{r registry}
catalogue <- statsnzreleases::statsnz_releases(include_unsupported = FALSE)
catalogue[, c("release_id", "release_name", "frequency", "supported")]
```

The `release_id` is the stable identifier used by
`read_statsnz_release()`. The catalogue records the release families, support
status, frequencies, and matching rules provided by this installed version.

## 2. Retrieve and chart a time series

The live workflow searches a bounded window in the official release calendar,
then passes the selected page URL to the public reader. The exact series and
period bounds make the requested table explicit. Run this chunk interactively
when official network access is available:

```{r live-read}
if (interactive()) {
  latest_cpi <- statsnzreleases::statsnz_latest_release(
    "nz_stats_cpi",
    as_of = as.Date("2026-08-24"),
    lookback_months = 2L
  )
  cpi_live <- statsnzreleases::read_statsnz_release(
    "nz_stats_cpi",
    release_url = latest_cpi$url[[1L]],
    series = c("CPIQ.SE9NS6000", "CPIQ.SE9NS6500"),
    start_period = "2016.03",
    end_period = "2026.06",
    quiet = TRUE
  )
  cpi_live[, c("series_reference", "period_date", "data_value")]
}
```

For deterministic offline rendering, this guide feeds an installed official
snapshot from [*Consumers price index: June 2026 quarter*](https://www.stats.govt.nz/information-releases/consumers-price-index-june-2026-quarter/)
through the same
public reader, attachment selector, parser, standardiser, filters, class, and
provenance path. Only the release-page lookup and download transport are
replaced. The snapshot contains 84 official quarterly observations for
`CPIQ.SE9NS6000` (Tradable All Groups) and `CPIQ.SE9NS6500` (Non-Tradable All
Groups) from March 2016 through June 2026. Its installed provenance record
documents the release and attachment URLs, full-file and extract hashes, and
extraction. The extract includes Stats NZ data licensed by Stats NZ for reuse
under CC BY 4.0; the installed record provides the full attribution.

```{r snapshot-output}
if (is.null(cpi)) {
  cat("Install the suggested package `testthat` to run the offline reader demonstration.\n")
} else {
  cpi[, c(
    "series_reference", "period", "data_value", "series_label", "release_id"
  )]
}
```

The returned object is a tibble with class `statsnz_release_data`.  Its core
columns include the release identity, series reference and label, period and
period date, numeric and raw values, units, and source attachment fields.
Filtering preserves the release provenance attribute.

The output is already long-form, so base row and column selection is sufficient
for plotting:

```{r chart-data, eval=!is.null(cpi)}
chart_data <- cpi[
  !is.na(cpi$period_date) & !is.na(cpi$data_value),
  c("period_date", "data_value", "series_label")
]
utils::head(chart_data, 4L)
```

```{r cpi-chart, eval=!is.null(cpi), fig.width=8, fig.height=4.8, dpi=120, out.width="100%", fig.alt="Line chart of New Zealand tradable and non-tradable CPI indexes from March 2016 to June 2026. Both rise after 2020, with the non-tradable index ending higher."}
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    chart_data,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = period_date, y = data_value,
      colour = series_label, group = series_label
    )
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line() +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = "Tradable and non-tradable consumer prices",
      subtitle = "Quarterly published observations",
      x = "Quarter",
      y = "CPI index",
      colour = "CPI series",
      caption = "Source: Stats NZ, Consumers price index: June 2026 quarter"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
}
```

## 3. Inspect provenance and the cache

Every downloaded attachment is represented in the provenance returned by
`statsnz_provenance()`.  The record includes the release page, retrieval time,
attachment URLs, local cache paths, byte sizes, and SHA-256 hashes.

```{r provenance, eval=TRUE}
if (!is.null(cpi)) {
  provenance <- statsnzreleases::statsnz_provenance(cpi)
  provenance[c("release_id", "release_name", "release_title", "release_url")]
  provenance$attachments[, c("name", "bytes", "sha256")]
}
```

The default cache location follows R's user-cache conventions through
`tools::R_user_dir()`.  It is outside the project source tree and is created
when a download needs it rather than during package loading.

```{r cache}
basename(statsnzreleases::statsnz_cache_dir())
```

Pass `cache_dir` explicitly when a workflow needs a managed cache location, and
use `refresh = TRUE` when you intentionally want to download the selected
attachments again. See [Reproducible reads](release-discovery-reproducibility.html)
for historical URLs, filtering, network boundaries, and cache guidance.
